$doc: MQ Research Gate — architecture & monetization atlas. A structured map for AI chats: components, databases, the access model, endpoints, phase status, the decision log, a file map, a glossary. Human view: docs/atlas.html (kept in step with this file). Feedback log: docs/feedback.json. Entry point for working on the code: CLAUDE.md.

app.name: MQ Research Gate
app.oneLiner: A detective's study for the Qur'an: meaning is earned from within the text (the organic Qur'anic methodology). Notice a word, open a case on its root family, gather every place the Book uses it, form a hypothesis, then weigh the classical dictionaries.
app.stack: React + Vite + TypeScript SPA (app/), opened in a browser at the research server's own address, in the desktop window, or from a local dev build. The research server (server/, Hono + Postgres + Better Auth) is the only server: the Qur'an corpus, every account's private research, accounts and the community, and the hosted MCP. MCP server (mcp/) lets an AI study and propose, as its user. corpus-core/ is the corpus code library that the research server runs. Electron desktop wrapper (electron/). mobile/ is a separate offline Android app that does not talk to the server.
app.run: Postgres + `npm run dev` (research server :8100 and web app :5174). First time: npm install, npm run server:migrate, npm run corpus:migrate, bootstrap/set-password. After pulling a new migration: npm run server:migrate (dev doesn't auto-migrate; Docker does).

principle.core: Roles say what you may DO; plans say what you may USE and READ. Your research is private to your account; only what you publish is shared, only once approved, and only with the audience it names.
principle.constraint: You can only enforceably charge for what the server holds.
principle.consequence: Everything lives on the research server: the corpus, every account's research (one schema, row-level security), the community. The app and the MCP read and write it as the signed-in user.

components.name: App
components.runtime: React 18 + Vite SPA — in a browser at https://<domain>/ (Caddy serves the build), in the desktop window, or a local build
components.role: Reads the corpus (${REMOTE_URL}/corpus) and reads/writes the reader's research (${REMOTE_URL}/research) with the session cookie; the community likewise. Nothing of the research is kept on the machine. Shows a lock or a read-only note for a plan feature the account can't use. A Guide screen walks through the app from the live account and plan. Maintainers get an Admin tab.

components.name: Corpus code (corpus-core/)
components.runtime: a library: corpus services + Hono route builders, over a SQLite or Postgres driver
components.role: The corpus code (search, roots, similarity, …) and its route builders, run by the research server over Postgres, and by the tests, the parity check and MQ_CORPUS=local over quran.db.

components.name: MCP
components.runtime: one MCP server (mcp/src/server.ts) over two transports: stdio (mcp/src/index.ts) and streamable HTTP hosted on the research server at /mcp (server/src/mcp-http.ts)
components.role: An AI studies the corpus and proposes into the reader's research, AS the reader (a personal API token). The server enforces the AI boundary on every token write, and a token can't publish, review or administer. Hosted: nothing to install, the client connects with a URL and the token. stdio with MQ_CORPUS=local reads quran.db instead; research is always the account's.

components.name: Research server
components.role: Auth (cookie or API token), open sign-up and invites, the role ladder, plan tiers, plan features and per-item rules, the corpus (/corpus), every account's research (/research, row-level security), the community with audiences, Admin endpoints, the hosted MCP (/mcp). Deployed with Docker + Caddy (DEPLOY.md).

components.name: Desktop
components.role: The desktop window: serves app/dist from a tiny built-in file server on localhost:51789 (a trusted origin) and opens a window at it. No back end, no data files.

components.name: Mobile (Android)
components.role: A separate reader app: the corpus bundled as on-device SQLite, its own ports of the corpus queries, its own on-device research.db. Not an npm workspace; no account, no server. Last worked on August 2026 (mobile/README.md).

corpus (Postgres schema `corpus`).access: read-only; each /corpus route belongs to one plan feature (the read-assist tools, free by default)
corpus (Postgres schema `corpus`).holds: Qur'an text in four scripts, per-word morphology (root/lemma/form), roots, ~10 classical lexicons, translations, search indexes. Copied from quran.db and verified exact.
corpus (Postgres schema `corpus`).load: npm run corpus:migrate (-- --verify to re-verify only). server/src/corpus/{schema,load,verify}.ts. 294,804 rows, 143.5 MB, 18 s.
corpus (Postgres schema `corpus`).collation: every text column COLLATE "C" (= SQLite BINARY) so Arabic sorts identically.
corpus (Postgres schema `corpus`).parity: npm run corpus:parity — the SAME corpus routes over each driver, compared over HTTP. Full sweep 2026-09-26: 77,439 requests (every chapter, verse, root, root pair, word, search) — all identical. --quick samples ~3k.

quran.db.holds: The same corpus in SQLite. The SOURCE for corpus:migrate, the local driver (MQ_CORPUS=local, tests, offline MCP), the parity reference and the mobile app's build input. The app does not read it.
quran.db.corrections: Signed, versioned patch files (CORPUS.md). The patch tool writes SQLite only; re-run corpus:migrate to carry a correction into Postgres.

research (Postgres, row-level security).access: private to its account; read-write by that account (and its AI, within the boundary). Writes need the record's plan feature; a locked feature is read-only.
research (Postgres, row-level security).location: the research server — schema `research`, shared, every row carrying its user_id
research (Postgres, row-level security).holds: cases + board layout, form_research + form_revisions, trails, notes, word_indications (+ refinements), user_root_meanings, motifs, comparisons, settings, and the outbox of what was published.
research (Postgres, row-level security).isolation: Row-level security, enabled and FORCED on every table, one policy: user_id = the request's user (app.user_id), for reads and writes. Requests SET LOCAL ROLE mqrg_research (not a superuser, no BYPASSRLS), set app.user_id via set_config with a bound parameter from the principal, and search_path to research — all LOCAL to the transaction. No user bound = nothing visible, nothing writable. A draft is reachable only by its owner (and their own AI); staff included. Deleting an account cascades to its research.
research (Postgres, row-level security).shape: Every row carries user_id, which leads every key (migrations/0010_research_rls.sql). The store's SQL names no user: RLS filters and the user_id default fills it in. author_id = the account id. Tests: research-store.test.ts (what it does), research-cloud.test.ts (cross-account SQL refused, RLS forced on every table, the AI boundary).
research (Postgres, row-level security).notProtectedAgainst: A database superuser (the operator) can read the tables directly, as in any hosted app.
research (Postgres, row-level security).noFile: Research lives only in the account: no research.db, no import/export (removed 2026-09-28; migration 0011 dropped the file-era owner table). Backed up with the database (deploy/backup.sh).

accessModel.rule: Roles say what you may do; plans say what you may use and read. Publishing needs both. Everything fails closed.

roles.ladder: DATA: table role_levels (name, rank, label, fixed). Seeded reader 0 · student 10 · researcher 20 · scholar 30 · moderator 80 · maintainer 100. reader, moderator and maintainer are FIXED (the staff powers hang on them); learner rungs sit between (rank 1–79) and are the maintainer's to add, rename, re-rank or remove.
roles.meaning: A person's standing — what they may DO. A principal carries its role's rank (loaded at sign-in), so guards compare ranks; unknown roles rank below everyone.

powers.publish (submit / propose): feature_access 'publish' — researcher by default, the maintainer's choice. Also needs plan feature 'publish' and a signed-in session.

roles.refusal: 401 signed out, 403 role too low. An API token is refused on every staff rung and on publishing: 'an API token can't do this. Sign in to the app instead.'

plans.ladder: DATA: table plan_tiers (name, rank, label). Seeded free (0) < pro (100); a maintainer adds e.g. student 50, scholar 200 in the Admin tab. free is always rank 0.
plans.meaning: What you may USE and READ. A higher rank unlocks everything a lower one does; a lapsed plan (users.plan_expires_at past) counts as free.

planFeatures.table: resource_access (kind, key, min_plan). Kinds: 'feature', 'translation', 'lexicon' (migration 0013 replaced the single 'corpus' and 'community' rules). min_plan = a tier, 'free' (= any signed-in account), or NULL (= public, no sign-in). A missing feature rule reads as pro.
planFeatures.list: 27 features, defined in code (server/src/plan-features.ts) — a new one needs a line there and its routes in the maps; nothing in the database.

groups.read (read-assist tools, default free): text, translations, search, roots, meanings, follow-root, follow-word, echoes, similar, spelling, wazn, linkages, lens, compare
groups.interact (the reader's own study, defaul: notes, indications, my-meanings, motifs, links, speakers, rules, characters

enforcement.corpus reads: Every /corpus route belongs to one feature (featureForCorpus; unmatched → text) and answers 401 / 402 by its rule (requireCorpusFeature). Meanings and translations ride inside other answers, so a locked one is also filtered out of those (corpus/serve.ts).
enforcement.the reader's records: A locked interaction or research feature is READ-ONLY: what they made stays visible, writes are refused (featureForResearch looks only at writes; requireResearchFeature).
enforcement.community: requirePlanFeature('community') on readings, claims, dissents; 'divergences' on POST /divergences; 'publish' on POST /submissions and /claims; 'ai' on minting a token and on the hosted MCP.

perItem.translation: key = resource id; below its tier the translation is LEFT OUT of results
perItem.lexicon: key = source (lanes_lexicon, lisan_ul_arab, …); below its tier the entries are left out of a root page
perItem.noRule: An item with no rule of its own needs only what its feature needs.

planFeatures.refusal: 401 {detail} if a sign-in is needed, 402 if a higher plan is.
planFeatures.cache: Rules are cached 10 s per process: a change applies at once on the instance that made it.
planFeatures.app: GET /me returns `features` (what the account may use); the app shows a lock or a read-only note (app/src/lib/features.ts, FeatureGate, PlanLock, PlanLockNotice).
planFeatures.file: server/src/plan-features.ts (FEATURES, featureForCorpus, featureForResearch), server/src/resource-access.ts (featureMin, featuresFor, canRead, requirePlanFeature, requireCorpusFeature, requireResearchFeature, itemFilter)

accessModel.edit: In the app: Admin → Roles (the ladder, 'What each role may do'), Plan tiers, What each plan may use, Translations, Dictionaries, People. Scripted: npm run access (show | tier | tier-remove | feature | translation | lexicon) / set-plan.
accessModel.billing: Not wired yet. A maintainer grants plans in the Admin tab (or set-plan / POST /plan). That is the single seam a payment provider slots into.
accessModel.staff: Staff (moderator and maintainer) pass every plan gate, whatever tier their account holds, and /me reports every feature as theirs. Learner rungs are not staff and still need the plan. One check, in canRead (server/src/resource-access.ts).

audiences.rule: Every published result (claim version, submission) carries an audience: at least a role AND at least a plan (either may be empty). The author proposes it; the reviewer confirms or changes it when approving/establishing. Nothing is visible before approval except to its author and staff.
audiences.enforcement: Every community read — claims, the group's reading, dissents, readings/chips, divergences and their count — filters by the viewer's role rank and plan. Authors always see their own; staff (moderator+) see everything, since they review it. The community plan feature still applies to all of it.
audiences.file: server/src/role-ladder.ts makeAudienceCheck; claims.ts takes a CanSee

auth.accounts: Created by our own code only (Better Auth's sign-up route is closed): open sign-up (POST /signup, server/src/signup.ts) makes a reader on the free plan with a validated profile — date of birth (age is derived), region (ISO country code), optional gender — at most 5 sign-ups an hour per address; redeeming an invite (POST /invites/redeem, server/src/invites.ts) makes an account at the invite's role (researcher when the maintainer named none). The first maintainer is bootstrapped from the CLI.
auth.signIn: Email + password. Magic link is still configured but needs an email transport. Forgotten passwords reset by email through the server's own /reset-password page.
auth.cookie: Better Auth session cookie — the app (credentials: 'include'). First-party for the hosted web app; SameSite=None; Secure over HTTPS for an app on localhost.
auth.apiTokens: Personal API tokens (mqrg_…, stored as SHA-256; secret shown once) for headless clients — the MCP. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer`, or in the path for the hosted MCP (/mcp/mqrg_…). Made in the app: Account → Connect an AI assistant (needs plan feature 'ai'). A token reads as its user, plan included, and may only propose: it can't publish, review, establish, administer or manage tokens. server/src/api-tokens.ts, session.ts, roles.ts.

corpusCode.oneCodebase: corpus-core/src/corpus-db.ts defines CorpusDb {query, one, scalar} (async). Every corpus service (content, roots, linkages, wazn, expressions, echoes, spellings, freetext, similarity, morphology) is written once against it.
corpusCode.services: createCorpusServices(db) in corpus-core/src/corpus-services.ts; warmCorpus builds the memoised indexes (the cloud warms them at startup).
corpusCode.routes: corpus-core/src/routes/{content,roots,similarity,echoes,corpus}.ts take (services, entitlements). The research server mounts them at /corpus (server/src/corpus/serve.ts) with the plan filters as entitlements; the tests mount the same builders over quran.db (corpus-core/test/corpus-app.ts).
portableSql: a total ORDER BY wherever order is visible
DISTINCT → GROUP BY … ORDER BY MIN(id)
nullable sort keys NULLS FIRST (ASC) / NULLS LAST (DESC)
Postgres int8 counts normalised to numbers
corpusCode.spellingVariants: corpus-core/src/spellings.ts: a word's variant group ignores case (a vowel mark, never a rasm letter); a hamza seat changed only by what is attached is not a variant. /chapters/:id/variants lists the unusual spellings per āyah (`positions`) and the variant words written the usual way there (`common`); /verses/:key/spelling marks with `here` the spelling that occurrence is written in. The reader's ✍ mark shows a word's other spellings above it.

clients.app: app/src/api/client.ts: CORPUS = ${REMOTE_URL}/corpus. A refused read announces itself (CORPUS_ACCESS_EVENT) and CorpusAccessBanner says why once, at the top: offline / sign in / needs the X plan — and 'Your access has changed, reload' after a sign-in or plan grant. A refused tool (one feature locked) gives a short notice or a lock instead of the whole-app banner.
clients.mcp: mcp/src/corpus-client.ts: CorpusReads with remoteReads (HTTP, default) and localReads (MQ_CORPUS=local). 401 → 'create a token', 402 → 'needs the X plan', unreachable → 'set REMOTE_URL or MQ_CORPUS=local'. corpus-core/test/mcp-remote-corpus.test.ts runs every corpus tool on both paths: byte-identical. Tools, prompts and the write boundary: MCP.md.
clients.mcpHosted: https://<domain>/mcp with `Authorization: Bearer mqrg_…` (Claude Code, Cursor), or https://<domain>/mcp/mqrg_… for clients that take only a URL (Claude's custom connectors). Stateless; reaches the corpus and research routes in-process with the caller's token.

phases.title: Monetization: entitlements, live community, gated publishing
Corpus → Postgres: move + verify the data
Plan tiers as data; then 'features are role-based, resources are plan-based'
phases.summary: plan_tiers; resource_access (corpus, community whole; translation, lexicon per item) replaces corpus_policy/translation_access; publishing is role-only. The whole-corpus and whole-community rules were later split into plan features (phase plan-features).

phases.title: Corpus → Postgres: port the readers
phases.summary: One corpus codebase, two drivers; the cloud serves ALL of it at /corpus. Full parity: 77,439 requests identical.

phases.title: Personal API tokens
The app reads the corpus from /corpus
The MCP reads the corpus from /corpus, as its user
phases.summary: Account → Connect an AI assistant mints the token. (Research was still local at this point; it moved to the account in phase research-cloud.)

phases.title: Admin tab in the app
phases.summary: Plan tiers, access rules, each translation and dictionary, people (role + plan). Maintainers only.

phases.title: Deployable: Docker on a VPS, HTTPS, SMTP password reset
phases.summary: Image build, config refusal, migrations on start, corpus load in the container, HTTPS via Caddy, reset flow, backup. deploy/update.sh pulls, backs up, rebuilds and waits for health.

phases.title: Research in Postgres, private per account
phases.summary: Research in Postgres only: one shared schema under row-level security; the app and the MCP read/write it as the user; the AI boundary enforced by the server. research.db, its SQLite driver, import/export and the local research routes removed (2026-09-28).

phases.title: Roles as data; audiences on published results
phases.summary: role_levels ladder (student, scholar, …), publishing's role configurable, every published result shown only to its audience (role + plan), proposed by the author and confirmed by the reviewer.

phases.title: One server; folders named for what they are
phases.summary: The local server removed; server/ → corpus-core/, remote/ → server/.

phases.title: The web app and the MCP hosted on the server's address
phases.summary: Caddy carries the built app (deploy/web.Dockerfile) and serves it at https://<domain>/, proxying every other path to the server; the server always trusts its own public origin. The MCP runs at /mcp over streamable HTTP with the token as a Bearer header or in the path. The site and the MCP carry the project logo.

phases.title: Open sign-up
phases.summary: Anyone can create a free reader account (POST /signup, migration 0012: date of birth, region, optional gender). Better Auth's own sign-up route stays closed; invites still work. Admin → People shows region, age and join date.

phases.title: Plan features: per feature, what each plan may use
phases.summary: The single corpus switch became 23 features in three groups (migration 0013), each with its own rule. /corpus routes answer by their feature; a locked interaction or research feature is read-only. /me reports what the account may use and the app shows locks. The hosted MCP checks the 'ai' feature.

phases.title: Tokens can't publish or review
phases.summary: requireRole refuses a token on every staff rung; both publishing routes require a signed-in session. Migration 0014 sets invites.role's default to researcher.

phases.title: Guide: an in-app walkthrough
phases.summary: app/src/screens/Guide.tsx (? in the top bar, a card on Home, ⌘K → Guide): short chapters that read the live account and plan features, so its locks match the Admin settings.

phases.title: Reader and spelling-variant fixes
phases.summary: Spelling variants group a word across its cases and show a word's other spellings above it; an attached hamza is not a variant. A jumped-to āyah stays on screen while the page settles; a recent trail on Home resumes at its latest hop.

phases.title: Docs consolidated
phases.summary: 2026-11-20: CLAUDE.md is the entry point; DESIGN.md (with the community rules), SERVER.md, CORPUS.md, MCP.md, DEPLOY.md, DESKTOP.md are the references. INSTRUCTIONS.md, SHARED_RESEARCH*.md, BACKEND_TS_MIGRATION.md, app/README.md and mobile/MOBILE_ACTION_PLAN.md were merged in or removed.

phases.title: Leftovers of the offline-first design removed
phases.summary: 2026-11-20: GET /pull, pull.ts and its diagnose CLI, POST /me/local-id and users.local_id, and the sync_cursors table (migration 0015) — nothing called them. The root .env.example for the archived Python pipeline went too.

phases.title: Staff pass every plan gate
phases.summary: 2026-11-20: canRead lets a moderator or maintainer through whatever their tier. The older requirePlan guard, unused since plan features, is removed, so there is one plan check.

phases.title: Reading the Book through its own links
phases.summary: 2026-11-20: a labelled Links button on every āyah opens what it shares with the rest of the Book, rarest first (corpus-core/src/links.ts), and starts the āyah lens; Rare links lists every marker that exactly 2–5 āyāt share; Search by grammar finds āyāt built the same way (corpus-core/src/constructions.ts). The reader saves links, leads and speaker tags (migration 0016) and sees them in My links with a coverage map of the 114 sūrahs. Each meaning and verdict in a case shows how many separate āyāt it rests on. The MCP gained find_links, list_rare_links, find_construction, my_links, propose_link, propose_speaker. Search is a top-level tab; the Study menu and the palette name every screen. Not yet committed or deployed when this was written.

phases.title: Checking a reading against the whole Book
phases.summary: 2026-11-20: eleven tools that list every place and record what the reader decides. Rule checks (a rule, what would prove it wrong, every place it covers marked fits, exception or unsure). Characters (names, titles and pronouns filed at places, potential until established). The āyah's Links panel became four tabs: Links, Speakers, Characters, Pronouns. Dialogue shows a sūrah as a script and lists speech openers not yet tagged; a speaker tag also records who else hears and whether the text states the speaker. A link can be a tension, open until settled. A case card counts for or against the reading, and a case says what would prove it wrong. From the corpus: every occurrence of a marker, shape or pattern; Spellings (229 words written more than one way); two āyāt word against word; a wording check for any Arabic text; grammar search by participle, verbal noun, verb form, attached pronoun, noun number and gender. Migration 0017. The MCP gained list_occurrences, list_spellings, find_speech_openers, find_pronouns, check_wording, compare_ayat, my_rule_checks, suggest_rule_marks, my_characters, propose_mentions. The Study menu is two columns: In the Book, Your study. A refresh keeps the reading place (#/read/19:47). Not yet committed or deployed when this was written.

phases.title: What a reading rests on, and the gaps of the checking tools
phases.summary: 2026-11-21: six tools from a lecture on what an interpreter needs, and the gaps left by the checking tools. A reference slip says what kind of work it cites, and a case shows one line counting its āyāt, the reader's observations and each kind of cited work. The root page shows the Book's use first, then the reader's meaning, then the dictionaries with author and date. Earlier versions: a replaced verdict, established meaning, root meaning or indication is kept with its date and the reader's reason (migration 0018, which also gives a mention a part and adds set-aside openers). Motif spread by sūrah and page; Supplications; Opening and close of a sūrah. Fixes: Check as a rule from Spellings, a root's page, a word's menu and grammar search; a character and a rule have an address; rare-link phrases list the same places as a rule (464 of 6,151 differed, now none); every verb of ن د و is a speech opener, a call where the text shows no speech, with No speech here and the reader's own opener roots; the two pronouns of one word are two places; spelling kinds are named and grammar endings kept apart; ة turned ت by an attached pronoun is no longer a spelling, so ٱمْرَأَتُ shows its seven places. Dialogue tags an opener in place. A jump into the reader from a Study screen, Search or a case leaves Back to …, and the screen left stays alive behind the reader. The top bar is two rows on a narrow screen. The MCP gained root_spread, find_supplications and surah_frame. Not yet committed or deployed when this was written.

phases.title: Billing provider
phases.summary: Slots into the plan grant with no rework of the gates.

decisions.decision: Research lives on the research server, private to each account — one shared schema under row-level security.
decisions.why: The maintainer's call, 2026-09-27 (first built schema-per-account, then switched to RLS at their request): one set of tables whatever the number of accounts, one migration, queries across people possible for staff tooling. A draft is its owner's alone. Cost: studying needs the server; a database superuser can read the tables, as in any hosted app.

decisions.decision: student and scholar are ROLES (standing), not plan tiers; plans stay about paying.
decisions.why: The maintainer's call. A published result can then say 'scholar role or higher AND pro plan'.

decisions.decision: The publisher proposes a result's audience; the reviewer confirms or changes it at approval.
decisions.why: The maintainer's call. The author knows who it's for; the reviewer is accountable for what the community sees.

decisions.decision: Every feature is role-based; every resource is plan-based.
decisions.why: Maintainer's call, 2026-09-26: 'it will be easier.' One question per gate: may you DO this (role), may you READ this (plan).
decisions.refinedBy: plan-features-per-feature (2026-09-29): what a plan unlocks is now a list of plan features, not two whole resources.

decisions.decision: A plan unlocks FEATURES, one rule each, in three groups (read-assist, interaction, research & publication); a locked interaction or research feature is read-only.
decisions.why: 2026-09-29: decide per feature what each plan may use, instead of one corpus switch. Defaults make every read-assist tool free to any signed-in account and keep the reader's own study and publishing on Pro. Read-only rather than hidden, so what a reader made stays visible when a plan lapses. Features are defined in code, so a new one needs no migration.

decisions.decision: Anyone can create a free reader account; an invite brings someone in at the invite's role.
decisions.why: 2026-09-29. Accounts are still created only by our own code (Better Auth's sign-up route stays closed), so the profile is validated before the account exists and sign-ups are rate-limited per address.

decisions.decision: An API token can never publish, review or establish — only a signed-in session can.
decisions.why: 2026-10-12: only the maintainer routes had refused tokens, so an AI assistant could publish and, for a moderator, review. An assistant reads as its user and suggests; a person decides.

decisions.decision: The web app and the MCP are served from the research server's own address.
decisions.why: 2026-09-28: nothing to install. Opening https://<domain>/ is the whole app, with an ordinary first-party sign-in cookie; an AI client connects to /mcp with a URL and a token. The stdio MCP stays for local and offline (MQ_CORPUS=local) use.

decisions.decision: The corpus lives in Postgres and the cloud serves it; the app and MCP read it from /corpus.
decisions.why: The maintainer's call. Makes the corpus a gateable resource. Cost: reading needs the research server (the banner says so; MQ_CORPUS=local keeps the MCP working offline).

decisions.decision: One corpus code path over a driver interface, not a Postgres twin.
decisions.why: A twin drifts. With one codebase, parity is a property of SQL portability, proven by comparing the same routes over both drivers.

decisions.decision: Administration is an Admin tab for maintainers, not only a CLI.
decisions.why: Maintainer's request. The CLI stays for scripting.

decisions.decision: The MCP authenticates with a personal API token and reads as its user.
decisions.why: A headless process can't hold a browser session; a revocable token keeps the plan gate honest for the AI too.

decisions.decision: A translation or lexicon above the caller's tier is left out, not refused.
decisions.why: One verse carries many translations; refusing the whole page for one locked item would be wrong.

decisions.decision: Community data is read live from the server, never mirrored to the reader's machine.
decisions.why: Mirroring puts it on the reader's disk, which makes it un-gateable.

decisions.decision: Moderators and maintainers pass every plan gate.
decisions.why: The maintainer's call, 2026-11-20, answering a question open since 2026-09-26. A moderator on the free plan could not list the claims they are there to review, because reading the community is a plan feature; a maintainer on free saw locks on what they administer. Staff are few and appointed, so nothing is given away. Learner rungs still pay.

decisions.decision: Plan is a separate axis from role.
decisions.why: A paying reader isn't a researcher, and a tier named 'admin' is only what's paid for.
decisions.refinedBy: staff-pass-plan-gates (2026-11-20): the one exception — staff pass plan gates.

decisions.decision: The last maintainer can't be demoted.
decisions.why: It would lock everyone out of administering the community.

decisions.decision: No research.db: research exists only in the account, in Postgres.
decisions.why: The maintainer's call, 2026-09-28: still in development, nothing important in the file, so keep one place and one code path. Dropped with it: the SQLite research driver, the local server's research routes, import/export and 'Bring it into my account', MQ_RESEARCH=local, the file's owner record. Cost: no offline research and no file copy — the database backup is the copy.

decisions.decision: No local server: the research server is the only server.
decisions.why: The maintainer's call, 2026-09-28 (keep things tidy): once research moved to the account, the local server (server/ on :8000, /api/v1) served only a health check and the desktop window. Removed its entry, its routes app, run-dev scripts and the Electron server bundle; the desktop app serves app/dist itself and ships no quran.db. npm run dev starts the research server and the web app; npm start previews the build on :8000. The corpus code stays — renamed server/ → corpus-core/ (the research server runs it).

decisions.decision: Folders named for what they are: server/ (was remote/) is the research server; corpus-core/ (was server/) is the corpus code.
decisions.why: The maintainer, 2026-09-28: with the local server gone, remote/ was the only server and server/ was not one. Env vars (REMOTE_URL, REMOTE_TOKEN, VITE_REMOTE_URL, REMOTE_BASE_URL, REMOTE_PORT) keep their names so existing MCP configs and deploy .env files still work.

decisions.decision: The repo's markdown is a clean, current working context, not a record of how things were built.
decisions.why: The maintainer, 2026-11-20: design, build-plan and migration docs were describing a system that no longer exists. Finished history belongs in git; a stale doc is merged or deleted rather than marked 'history'.

decisions.decision: The link tools only find and count. They never state what a link means or who a character is.
decisions.why: The maintainer, 2026-11-20, after a lecture on reading the Qur'an through its internal cross-references: conclusions are subjective and are the reader's to argue in a case; the app and the assistant assist. So a link carries a count of the āyāt that share it, widespread markers are counted but not listed, and the evidence count reminds without blocking.

decisions.decision: A saved link, a lead and a speaker tag are the reader's own research records, not corpus data.
decisions.why: Which two places belong together, and who is speaking, are readings. They live in the account under row-level security (research.links, research.speech), an assistant may only propose them, and they get their own plan features (links, speakers).

decisions.decision: The āyah lens is started from a labelled Links button on every āyah, not only from the reader's menu.
decisions.why: The maintainer found the lens hidden and hard to use. The panel that lists an āyah's links is where a reader decides to follow it, so the lens starts there with one sentence saying what it does.

decisions.decision: Who a name, title or pronoun points to is recorded as a mention of a character the reader created, potential until the reader establishes it.
decisions.why: The maintainer, 2026-11-20: characters should exist as things, with pronouns and titles pointing to them as potential or established, the words the app already uses for meanings. The app never says who is who; an assistant can only file potential mentions.

decisions.decision: A rule check lists every place the rule covers and records the reader's mark on each; it never says the rule holds.
decisions.why: From a lecture on who a scholar is (falsifiability): the Book is a closed text, so every place can be looked at and one exception breaks a rule. The tool makes the counter-example findable and unmissable; the judgment on each place stays the reader's, and an assistant's marks wait as suggestions.

decisions.decision: The corpus answers 'where does this occur'; the research records 'what the reader decided there'. A rule's and a character's scope is a corpus query, not a stored list of places.
decisions.why: Keeps the corpus read-only and the same for everyone, and keeps a rule or a name honest: the places are always the Book's full list, so nothing unmarked can be forgotten.

decisions.decision: While the app is a prototype, the reader and its panels may be reshaped for ease, not only added to.
decisions.why: The maintainer, 2026-11-20. Applied at once: the Links panel became tabs, and the Study menu two grouped columns.

decisions.decision: The earlier text of a verdict, an established meaning, a root meaning or an indication is kept by the server when it is replaced, only if it had stood for ten minutes, and at most once per edit.
decisions.why: The app saves while the reader types, so the client cannot say what an earlier version is; without the ten-minute rule every keystroke would be one. The reader may add why they changed it, or remove an entry. An assistant can read them and change none.

decisions.decision: A case counts what it rests on (āyāt for and against, the reader's observations, and cited works by kind) and shows the count; it never ranks or warns.
decisions.why: From a lecture on what an interpreter needs: know what is the Book and what is a later source. The reader sees how much of a reading stands on the Book itself; whether that is enough is theirs to say.

decisions.decision: A letter that the script changes because something is attached is not a spelling variant: a hamza's seat, and ة written ت before a pronoun. A difference only in a grammatical ending is kept apart from spellings.
decisions.why: The maintainer, 2026-11-21: ٱمْرَأَتُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ was missing from Spellings. It was hidden because words were compared only in the same state, while pronoun-carrying words (ٱمْرَأَتُهُ) were counted as the ت spelling. Now the ت spelling is the seven places written with nothing attached. Later the same day: where the bare word is written both ways, the pronoun-carrying words are counted with neither spelling (ٱمْرَأَت: ت 7, ة 4, with a pronoun 13), so a spelling's count is the places it was written by choice.

decisions.decision: Any jump from a screen into the reader leaves a way back to that screen, at the place that was left; the screen stays alive behind the reader.
decisions.why: The maintainer, 2026-11-21: Tag it in the reader took them out of Dialogue with no way back. Tagging also became possible in place.

decisions.decision: A word is one entry in Spellings, and a rule started from one of its spellings lists exactly the places that entry counts.
decisions.why: The maintainer, 2026-11-21: كِتَٰب stood as two cards (with ٱل, without), and a rule from a card listed other places than the card (145 of 390 rows differed: the rule matched any word written with those letters, إِنَّ 2,145 for a row of 1). Inflections of one word that write the stem alike are now joined (180 entries became 173), and the rule's scope names the entry and the spelling.

glossary.role: A person's standing on the ladder (reader < student < researcher < scholar < moderator < maintainer). Decides what they may DO: publish, review, establish, administer.
glossary.plan / tier: What an account has paid for — a rung on the plan ladder (plan_tiers). Decides what it may USE and READ. Higher rank unlocks more.
glossary.plan feature: One of 23 things a plan can unlock (text, search, notes, cases, community, ai, …), each with one rule. Locked corpus reads answer 402; a locked feature over the reader's own records is read-only.
glossary.min_plan: A rule's requirement: a tier, 'free' (signed in), or NULL (public).
glossary.feature_access: The table that holds which ROLE publishing needs (researcher by default). Not to be confused with plan features.
glossary.API token: mqrg_… — a revocable credential that reads as its user and may only propose; how the MCP signs in.
glossary.AI boundary: What a token request may do to a reader's research: add its own tagged proposals, change only what it added, never set a primary gloss, a verdict or an established meaning.
glossary.locally established: A form meaning YOU established, in your own research.
glossary.globally established: The reading reviewers accepted as the group's; lives on the server.
glossary.claim: One author's reading of one subject (a form or a root), with its argument; successive readings are versions of it.
glossary.dissent: A recorded disagreement with a globally established reading, preserved not resolved.
glossary.divergence (⚖): A form you established whose meaning differs from the group's. Computed live on the server ('Where I stand apart').
glossary.audience: Who may see a published result: at least a role and at least a plan. Proposed by the author, confirmed by the reviewer.
glossary.role ladder: reader < student < researcher < scholar < moderator < maintainer — data the maintainer edits; the three fixed rungs carry the staff powers.
glossary.link (marker): Something two or more āyāt share: a phrase of three or more words, two adjacent words, a written word, a dictionary form or a root. Its rarity is the number of āyāt that carry it; a marker in two āyāt ties exactly those two.
glossary.saved link / lead: A link the reader keeps between two word spans, with what they share, a kind, a group name and a note. With only one end it is a lead: noticed, the other end still to find.
glossary.speaker tag: The reader's record of who speaks in a span of an āyah and to whom. The corpus does not say, so it is research, not corpus data.
glossary.rule check: A rule the reader states, what they say would prove it wrong, and a mark on each place it covers: fits, exception or not sure. The places come from the corpus, complete.
glossary.character / mention: A character is someone the reader names. A mention points one place at a character as a name, title, description or pronoun; it is potential until the reader establishes it.
glossary.tension: A saved link of the kind 'these two seem to disagree, to me'. Open until the reader settles it and says how.
glossary.speech opener: A word that introduces speech (قال، قالوا، قل، نادى). The corpus finds them; who speaks is the reader's speaker tag.
glossary.earlier version: A text the reader replaced (a verdict, an established meaning, a root meaning, an indication), kept with its date and, if they say, why they changed it.
glossary.rests on: The count of what stands behind a case: āyāt for and against, the reader's observations, and cited works by kind (dictionary, tafsīr, narration, outside story).
glossary.part (of a mention): Which pronoun of a word a mention points at: 0 is the word itself, 1, 2 … the pronouns in the corpus's order.

notice: After migration 0013 the read-assist tools are free to any signed-in account, while the reader's own study (notes, indications, my meanings, motifs) and research & publication (cases, publish, community, divergences, the AI assistant) default to pro. Moderators and maintainers pass every plan gate, so staff never see those locks; grant plans to everyone else in Admin → People, or relax a rule in Admin → What each plan may use.

deployment.shape: One Linux VPS, docker compose (deploy/): Postgres 16 + the research server (server/Dockerfile) + Caddy (automatic HTTPS), which also carries the built web app (deploy/web.Dockerfile) and serves it at https://<domain>/, proxying every other path to the server. Only 80/443 exposed.
deployment.container: entrypoint: serve (config check → migrations → server) | migrate | corpus-migrate | corpus-parity | bootstrap | set-password | set-plan | test-users | access | smoke
deployment.update: deploy/update.sh — pulls main (or a named branch), backs up, rebuilds and waits for health.
deployment.safety: NODE_ENV=production refuses to start without a real AUTH_SECRET, DATABASE_URL, an https REMOTE_BASE_URL, or with SMTP chosen but unset (config.ts deployProblems).
deployment.cookies: The hosted web app is on the server's own address, so its sign-in is a first-party cookie and the server always trusts its own public origin. For an app on localhost or the desktop window, the session cookie is SameSite=None; Secure over HTTPS.
deployment.email: SMTP (nodemailer, src/mailer.ts): password reset (app: Account → Email me a reset link → the server's /reset-password page) and magic links. console transport prints them.
deployment.backups: deploy/backup.sh — nightly pg_dump, 14 days; copy off the machine.
deployment.appBuild: The hosted web app is built by docker compose with the right address. The desktop app and a local `npm start` learn it at build time: VITE_REMOTE_URL=https://<domain>.
